name: AD9910BSVZ-REEL
title: AD9910: 1 GSPS, 14-bit direct digital synthesizer with RAM, ramp generator and parallel port, TQFP-100 EP
summary: A direct digital synthesizer clocked at up to 1 GSPS with an on-chip 14-bit DAC, producing sine waves up to 400 MHz with a 32-bit tuning word (about 0.23 Hz steps at 1 GSPS), 16-bit phase offset and 14-bit amplitude control. Frequency, phase and amplitude can come from eight profiles, a 1024 × 32-bit RAM, a linear ramp generator or an 18-bit parallel port, with output shift keying for amplitude ramps. The reference comes from a direct clock, a crystal or a 12× to 127× PLL multiplier; control is by a serial port. Supplies are 1.8 V and 3.3 V; AD9910BSVZ and AD9910BSVZ-REEL both carry the -40°C to +85°C range and the 100-lead exposed-pad TQFP (SV-100-4).
key_figures: 14-bit, full-scale current 8.6 mA to 31.6 mA (20 mA typ)
−84 dBc to −96 dBc typ (50.1 MHz to 401.3 MHz)
−152 dBc/Hz typ at 1 kHz offset, 20 MHz out, multiplier off
715 mW typ single tone; 19 mW typ full sleep

pins.function: 1.8 V digital core supply; its current rises in proportion to system clock frequency.

pins.name: AGND
pins.function: Analog ground.

pins.name: DGND
pins.function: Digital ground.

pins.name: SYNC_IN+
pins.function: LVDS sync input, true side, rising edge active: the master's sync signal that aligns the internal clocks. 100 Ω termination across SYNC_IN+ and SYNC_IN− on chip.

pins.name: SYNC_IN−
pins.function: LVDS sync input, complement side.

pins.name: SYNC_OUT+
pins.function: LVDS sync output, true side, rising edge active: carries this device's clock state to slave devices.

pins.name: SYNC_OUT−
pins.function: LVDS sync output, complement side.

pins.name: SYNC_SMP_ERR
pins.function: High when the sync receiver did not get a valid sample of SYNC_IN.

pins.name: MASTER_RESET
pins.function: Active high reset: every memory element is cleared and registers go back to their defaults.

pins.name: EXT_PWR_DWN
pins.function: Active high: enters the power-down mode selected by CFR1[3]. Tie to ground when unused.

pins.name: PLL_LOCK
pins.function: High when the REFCLK PLL is locked to the reference; latched.

pins.name: RAM_SWP_OVR
pins.function: High when a RAM sweep profile has finished.

pins.name: D[15:0]
pins.function: 16-bit parallel data input, active high: D15 on pin 25 down to D0 on pin 48.

pins.name: F[1:0]
pins.function: Parallel port destination bits (F1 pin 49, F0 pin 50): choose what the parallel word modulates.

pins.name: PDCLK
pins.function: Parallel data clock at a quarter of the DAC sample rate; parallel data is aligned to it.

pins.name: TxENABLE
pins.function: Active high gate for parallel data: in burst use it marks valid words; in continuous use it stays high.

pins.name: PROFILE[2:0]
pins.function: Select one of eight profiles (PROFILE2 pin 52, PROFILE1 pin 53, PROFILE0 pin 54). A change also moves the I/O buffers into the active registers; set up to SYNC_CLK.

pins.name: SYNC_CLK
pins.function: System clock divided by 4; I/O_UPDATE and PROFILE[2:0] are set up to its rising edge.

pins.name: I/O_UPDATE
pins.function: Active high: moves the I/O buffer contents into the active registers. Becomes an output when the internal I/O update is on.

pins.name: OSK
pins.function: Output shift keying control. Manual mode: low forces amplitude to 0, high gives the programmed scale factor. Automatic mode: low ramps the amplitude down to zero, high ramps it up to the scale factor.

pins.name: DROVER
pins.function: Goes high when the digital ramp generator is at its upper or lower limit.

pins.name: DRCTL
pins.function: Sets the ramp direction of the digital ramp generator (high = rising). Tie low when the DRG is unused.

pins.name: DRHOLD
pins.function: High freezes the digital ramp generator. Tie low when the DRG is unused.

pins.name: SDIO
pins.function: Serial data: bidirectional by default (2-wire), input only in 3-wire mode.

pins.name: SDO
pins.function: Serial data output, active only in 3-wire (unidirectional) mode; leave open in bidirectional mode.

pins.name: SCLK
pins.function: Serial clock: writes clock in on the rising edge, reads clock out on the falling edge.

pins.name: CSB
pins.function: Chip select, active low (CS with an overbar). Low lets the part respond to SCLK; high makes it ignore the serial pins and puts SDO and SDIO at high impedance. May be tied low when the host controls SCLK.

pins.name: I/O_RESET
pins.function: Active high: aborts a serial cycle and resets the port state machine without touching the registers. Tie to ground when unused.

pins.name: IOUTB
pins.function: Complementary DAC current output (IOUT with an overbar), open drain. Terminate with 50 Ω to AGND.

pins.name: IOUT
pins.function: DAC current output, open drain. Terminate with 50 Ω to AGND.

pins.name: DAC_RSET
pins.function: Sets the DAC reference current; connect 10 kΩ to AGND.

pins.name: REF_CLK
pins.function: Reference clock input, true side; also one crystal terminal when the internal oscillator is used.

pins.name: REF_CLKB
pins.function: Reference clock input, complement side (REF_CLK with an overbar); the other crystal terminal.

pins.name: REFCLK_OUT
pins.function: Buffered copy of the reference (crystal) clock, available with the PLL enabled.

pins.name: XTAL_SEL
pins.function: 1.8 V logic: high (to AVDD 1.8 V) turns on the internal crystal oscillator. Tie to AGND when unused.

pins.name: EPAD
pins.function: Exposed pad; solder to ground.

circuits.title: Crystal connection
circuits.description: A fundamental-mode crystal of about 25 MHz sits across REF_CLK and REF_CLKB, with a 39 pF capacitor from each crystal terminal to ground, so the internal oscillator generates the reference. The oscillator runs when XTAL_SEL is driven high with 1.8 V logic.

circuits.title: Direct drive from a differential source
circuits.description: A PECL, LVPECL or LVDS driver feeds both reference inputs through 0.1 µF coupling capacitors, with the driver's own termination network across the pair ahead of the capacitors. The capacitors keep the inputs at their internal bias of about 1.35 V.

circuits.title: Single-ended source to differential input through a balun
circuits.description: A 50 Ω single-ended source drives the primary of a 1:1 balun; the secondary, loaded by 50 Ω, drives REF_CLK and REF_CLKB through 0.1 µF capacitors.

circuits.title: Single-ended source to single-ended input
circuits.description: A 50 Ω single-ended source, terminated by 50 Ω to ground, drives REF_CLK through 0.1 µF; REF_CLKB is returned to ground through its own 0.1 µF capacitor.

circuits.title: REFCLK PLL external loop filter
circuits.description: The REFCLK PLL's loop filter hangs from the PLL_LOOP_FILTER pin to the AVDD supply: a series C1 and R1 branch in parallel with C2. This makes a third-order, type II loop. The values are the worked example for ICP = 287 µA, KV = 625 MHz/V, N = 25, 50 kHz loop bandwidth and 45° phase margin; the loop filter equations give values for other settings. The AVDD side ties directly to pin 3.

circuits.title: DDS in PLL feedback locking to a reference
circuits.description: An external PLL (AD9510, AD9511 or ADF4106) compares a divided reference with the divided, filtered output of the AD9910. Its charge pump and loop filter steer a VCO, and the VCO output is both the system output and the AD9910's REF_CLK. The DDS in the feedback path gives fine frequency and delay tuning of the locked VCO.

parts.note: dividers, phase comparator and charge pump

circuits.title: Synchronizing multiple devices with AD9510 clock distribution
circuits.description: Four AD9910s (one master, three slaves) share a reference from an AD9510 clock distributor with delay equalization, fed by a clock source. The master's SYNC_OUT goes to a second AD9510 that equalizes delay and returns a sync signal to the SYNC_IN of every device, the master included. Each device has its own FPGA that sends parallel data and takes back SYNC_CLK; a central controller talks to all four FPGAs. The four analog outputs are A1 to A4.

circuits.title: Clock generation with an AD9512 to AD9515 clock distribution chip
circuits.description: A reference clock drives the AD9910; its DAC output passes a low-pass filter into an AD9512, AD9513, AD9514 or AD9515, which divides it by 1 to 32 with adjustable delay and delivers n LVPECL, LVDS or CMOS clock outputs, n depending on the chip chosen.

operation.text: A 32-bit phase accumulator, 16-bit phase offset and 14-bit amplitude scaling drive an angle-to-amplitude converter whose sine or cosine output (CFR1[16]) goes, optionally through the inverse sinc filter, to the 14-bit current-output DAC. The three DDS parameters (frequency, phase, amplitude) come from the profile registers, the RAM, the digital ramp generator, the parallel port or the OSK block, depending on what is enabled. Tuning resolution at 1 GSPS is about 0.23 Hz.

Four sources can supply the DDS parameters: single tone (profile registers), RAM modulation, digital ramp modulation and parallel data port modulation, plus OSK for amplitude. They can be on at once; when two drive the same parameter, a fixed priority decides (see Data source priority).

Eight profile registers each hold a frequency, phase and amplitude. PROFILE[2:0] selects one; a change takes effect at the next SYNC_CLK rising edge. With RAM enabled the same eight addresses hold RAM profiles instead. Two-tone FSK, for example, puts the space FTW in Profile 0 and the mark FTW in Profile 1 and drives PROFILE0 with the bit stream.
Any modulation of the DDS parameters runs at no more than fSYSCLK/4, so the modulation carries images at multiples of fSYSCLK/4.

18 bits: D[15:0] carry an unsigned data word and F[1:0] say where it goes (amplitude, phase, frequency or polar). PDCLK runs at a quarter of the DAC rate and latches data on its rising edge by default (polarity set by CFR2[10], output turned off by CFR2[11], in which case it stays low but still times the port internally). TxENABLE gates the data (polarity set by CFR2[9]); while it is false the port either feeds zeros or holds its last value, by CFR2[6]. TxENABLE may instead be clocked at the data rate, meeting setup and hold each cycle. For frequency, the 16-bit word is an offset added to the FTW, shifted left one place per step of the 4-bit FM gain.

The DAC delivers its current on a balanced pair, IOUT and IOUTB. RSET from DAC_RSET to AGND sets the reference current, 10 kΩ recommended, and the 8-bit auxiliary DAC (FSC) scales the full-scale current. The load must keep the output voltage inside the compliance range: beyond it distortion rises and the output stage can be damaged.

A 7-tap FIR filter ahead of the DAC (CFR1[22]) compensates the sin(x)/x roll-off, which reaches about 4 dB at Nyquist. It flattens the response to within ±0.05 dB up to about 40% of the sample rate and costs about 3.0 dB of insertion loss.

REF_CLK/REF_CLKB take a differential or single-ended clock, or a crystal across the pins. Direct inputs up to 2 GHz are accepted; above 1 GHz the input divider must be on. Drive both pins through 0.1 µF capacitors so the internal bias of about 1.35 V is left alone; the input resistance is about 2.5 kΩ differential (1.2 kΩ single-ended), so the termination can match the source impedance. With the PLL on, REFCLK_OUT repeats the reference (crystal) frequency, with drive strength set by CFR3[29:28].
The on-chip oscillator works with fundamental-mode crystals only, with a resonant frequency near 25 MHz, and it is turned on by a 1.8 V logic high on XTAL_SEL.

The PLL multiplies the reference by 12 to 127 and its VCO limits the system clock to 420 MHz ≤ fSYSCLK ≤ 1 GHz. One of six VCO ranges must be chosen in CFR3[26:24] to contain fSYSCLK. Across the whole population and all conditions the needed range can differ between parts at one frequency (for instance 900 MHz may need 100b on one part at −10°C and 101b on another at 90°C); a frequency inside one of the skew-inclusive ranges needs the same setting on every part. For any single part the ranges overlap with no gaps. Charge pump current is set by CFR3[21:19].
PLL_LOCK goes high when the PLL locks and is latched. With the PLL bypassed it may stay high. Setting the PFD reset bit clears it; the bit must be cleared again for normal operation.

OSK controls the output amplitude and overrides every other amplitude source when enabled (CFR1[9]). In manual mode (CFR1[8] = 0) the amplitude follows the ASF scale factor, written over the serial port, and with CFR1[23] set the OSK pin forces it to zero when low. In automatic mode the OSK pin starts a linear ramp: high ramps from zero up to the ASF maximum, low ramps back down to zero, in steps of 1, 2, 4 or 8 LSB at intervals set by the 16-bit ramp rate clocked at fSYSCLK/4. A ramp reversed midway does not reach its end value. The ramp timer reloads when auto OSK is switched on, when the OSK pin changes, and on I/O updates if CFR1[10] is set. The OSK output starts at zero at power-up and is reset whenever OSK or auto OSK is cleared.

A 32-bit accumulator, stepped by a 16-bit timer clocked at fSYSCLK/4, ramps frequency (all 32 bits), phase (16 MSBs) or amplitude (14 MSBs), chosen by CFR2[21:20]. Upper and lower limits, rising and falling step sizes and rising and falling step intervals are each programmable; the upper limit must be above the lower. DRCTL sets the direction (high rises, low falls) and DRHOLD freezes the ramp. Parameters that are not the ramp's destination come from the active profile. The timer reloads when the DRG is enabled, when DRCTL changes and, with CFR1[15], on I/O updates. Clearing the accumulator puts the output at the lower limit; autoclear does so for one DDS clock and lets the ramp continue.

Normally the ramp stays at a limit once reached. With no-dwell high the output jumps from the upper limit straight to the lower; with no-dwell low it jumps from the lower to the upper. In no-dwell operation DRCTL acts on edges only: a rising edge starts a full rising ramp that ignores DRCTL until the limit (falling edge for no-dwell low). With both bits set the ramp runs continuously between the limits and a DRCTL edge just reverses direction. DROVER is high while the output sits at either limit, or, with the two no-dwell bits both set, pulses for two DDS clocks at each limit.

1024 words of 32 bits, with load/retrieve and playback modes. Set RAM enable to 0 while loading or reading it: program a RAM profile's start and end addresses (end above start), select that profile on the PROFILE pins, then write or read address 0x16. Each of the eight RAM profiles holds a 10-bit start and end address, a 16-bit address step rate, a 3-bit mode, a no-dwell high bit and a zero-crossing bit; address ranges may overlap. Playback needs RAM enable = 1 and routes words by CFR1[30:29] to frequency, phase, amplitude or polar (16 bits phase, 14 bits amplitude); unrouted parameters come from the FTW, POW and ASF registers. Serial access to the RAM interrupts any playback in progress. RAM_SWP_OVR is held low while RAM is disabled.

A profile selects a single RAM word, at its start address, which is applied to the parameter; so eight profiles give FSK, PSK or ASK with as many as eight levels, and any subset of the profile pins can be used for two- or four-level keying. RAM_SWP_OVR stays low. With the zero-crossing bit and phase as destination, a new phase is applied only when the phase accumulator wraps through zero, so BPSK jumps of 180° occur with little amplitude step.

Once started by an I/O update or a profile change, the addresses run from start to end at the profile's rate, then the state machine stops at the end (or back at the start with no-dwell high) and RAM_SWP_OVR goes high. A profile change resets RAM_SWP_OVR and starts the new waveform.

With CFR1[20:17] non-zero the profiles are sequenced internally from Profile 0 upward, ignoring the PROFILE pins, the per-profile mode bits and no-dwell high; burst codes stop after the last profile and continuous codes go back to Profile 0. RAM_SWP_OVR pulses for two DDS clocks at the end of each profile.

Uses Profile 0 only and ignores PROFILE[2:1]. PROFILE0 high counts the address up to the end address, low counts it down to the start; a change before reaching an end restarts the timer and reverses direction. RAM_SWP_OVR goes high at the end address and stays high until the start address is reached and PROFILE0 rises again.

operation.topic: RAM continuous bidirectional and recirculate modes
operation.text: Continuous bidirectional mode sweeps up and down between the addresses without stopping and toggles RAM_SWP_OVR at each end. Continuous recirculate mode runs start to end and jumps back to start, repeating, with a two-DDS-clock RAM_SWP_OVR pulse each time the end address is reached. In both, a profile change aborts the waveform and starts the newly selected one.

Serial writes land in a buffer; an I/O_UPDATE rising edge (pulse longer than one SYNC_CLK period) or a PROFILE change moves them into the active registers. SYNC_CLK is SYSCLK divided by 4; an I/O_UPDATE meeting setup to it gives a fixed pipeline latency to the DAC, otherwise the latency varies by one SYNC_CLK period. With CFR2[23] set, updates are generated internally and I/O_UPDATE becomes an output pulse, the rate set by CFR2[15:14] and the 32-bit I/O update rate register.

Four blocks can be powered down separately by CFR1 bits with EXT_PWR_DWN low: digital core, DAC, auxiliary DAC and REFCLK input. With the digital core down the serial port cannot update registers, but the digital power-down bit itself can still be cleared. EXT_PWR_DWN high powers down all four regardless of the bits, as a full power-down or, by CFR1[3], a fast recovery power-down that keeps the DAC bias, PLL, VCO and clock input running for a quick wake-up.

Devices are synchronized when their internal clock states match. The sync generator (one master) outputs fSYSCLK/16 on SYNC_OUT, aligned to the rising or falling SYSCLK edge and delayable in steps of about 75 ps. Each sync receiver samples the delayed SYNC_IN edge with its SYSCLK and presets its clock generator to the programmed 6-bit state. This needs edge-aligned REF_CLK at every device and an edge-aligned SYNC_IN at every device, the master included; equal receiver delays and preset values then give matching clock states. A setup and hold check, window set in steps of about 75 ps, flags timing failures on SYNC_SMP_ERR; at 1 GHz SYSCLK a window value of 4 (300 ps) suits, while too large a value gives false errors and too small may be unstable.

The supplies fall in four groups (digital and analog at each of 1.8 V and 3.3 V), each bypassed with 0.1 µF or 0.01 µF in parallel with 10 µF. DVDD_I/O pins are grouped; their current follows serial port activity. AVDD (3.3V) pins draw about 28 mA of bias current that does not change with frequency; isolate them from other 3.3 V rails with at least a ferrite bead, ideally a separate regulator. DVDD (1.8V) pins are grouped; current rises linearly with system clock and about 5% from 50 MHz to 400 MHz output. AVDD (1.8V) pin 3 feeds the PLL and the loop filter returns to it; for best PLL performance give it its own regulator, otherwise share pins 89 and 92's regulator through a ferrite bead. Pins 89 and 92 feed the REFCLK input; isolate them from other 1.8 V rails with at least a ferrite bead. Pin 6 may share the DVDD 1.8 V supply, through a ferrite bead for best performance.

A synchronous port, 2-wire (SDIO bidirectional, default) or 3-wire (SDIO in, SDO out, CFR1[1]), MSB first by default or LSB first (CFR1[0], which then applies to the instruction byte too). Each cycle is an instruction byte (read/write bit and 5-bit address) followed by all the bytes of that register; data is clocked in on SCLK rising edges and out on falling edges, and reads return the active registers. Reading a profile register needs the PROFILE pins set to that profile; writing does not. I/O_RESET aborts a cycle: complete bytes already written are kept, partial ones are lost, and the next byte is taken as an instruction. CS high suspends a cycle until it returns low.
